history.mdHelp.title: Markdown Sessions - Sync Across Devices
history.mdHelp.intro: This tab lists sessions exported as Markdown files in your workspace cc-exports folder. Because they are plain files in your repo, git carries them to every machine you work on - and to your teammates.
history.mdHelp.stepExportBody: Open any session and click Export, or right-click a session and choose Select Sessions to bulk-export. Files are written to cc-exports.
history.mdHelp.stepExportTip: Enable the .source.jsonl sidecar option during export for perfect, lossless resume.
history.mdHelp.stepCommitBody: cc-exports travels with your repo like any other file. Dropbox, iCloud, or any file sync works too.
history.mdHelp.stepPullBody: Exported sessions appear right here in the MD tab automatically - browsable and readable like any normal session.
history.mdHelp.stepResumeBody: Right-click and choose Resume. With a sidecar, the original session is restored losslessly with the same session ID. Without one, it is rebuilt from the Markdown with file paths remapped to this machine - even across Windows and macOS/Linux.

history.mdHelp.useBackups: Durable backups that survive the CLI automatic history cleanup

history.mdHelp.upgradeReason: The Free plan includes {limit} session exports. Upgrade to Pro for unlimited markdown export and cross-device session sync.
history.archiveHelp.title: Archived Sessions - Survive Auto-Cleanup
history.archiveHelp.intro: Claude Code and Codex silently delete old session transcripts after a retention period. Archiving keeps a backup copy in a folder neither CLI touches - so the sessions you care about stay viewable and resumable forever.
history.archiveHelp.stepArchiveBody: Right-click any session and choose Archive Session, or click the archive icon on the session row. A backup copy is saved instantly.
history.archiveHelp.stepKeepBody: The session stays in your normal list with an archive badge. Use the Sync button on this tab, or archive the session again, to capture messages added since the backup was made.
history.archiveHelp.stepDeletesTitle: When the CLI deletes the original
history.archiveHelp.stepDeletesBody: The session lives on in this Archived tab - fully viewable, across all your projects.
history.archiveHelp.stepResumeBody: Hit Resume and the backup is restored to its original location automatically, so claude -r or codex resume can find it again.
history.archiveHelp.goodRestore: Unarchiving removes the backup - but restores the original first if it was deleted, so you never lose the last copy.
history.archiveHelp.goodLocation: Archive location is configurable via the claude-history.archiveDirectory setting.
history.archiveHelp.goodOpenCode: OpenCode sessions cannot be archived yet because they live in a database, not files.

history.hooks.title: Real-Time Hooks
history.hooks.intro: Opt in to instant session status by adding lightweight hook entries to the CLI configs. The hooks append local event JSON to ~/.claude-history-viewer/hook-events.jsonl so the history list can show working, waiting for permission, and done states without waiting for file polling.
history.hooks.localNote: Local only. Disabling removes the hook entries and deletes the event log (~/.claude-history-viewer/hook-events.jsonl), so any leftover hook command becomes a harmless no-op.

mcp.header.title: ccassist MCP
mcp.header.subtitle: Manage local session-context access for your CLI agents.
mcp.intro.description1: ccassist is a local MCP server that exposes your chat history — Claude Code, Codex, Grok, and OpenCode sessions — to any AI CLI. An agent can search past sessions, grep tool outputs, pull a distilled context block to continue work from another session, and inspect the file changes a session made.
mcp.intro.description2: Everything runs on 127.0.0.1; your history never leaves this machine. One VS Code window serves the port, others stand by and take over automatically when it closes.
mcp.manual.description: Any MCP-capable client can connect — register a server named "ccassist" with transport "streamable HTTP" pointing at the endpoint above. Typical JSON config:
mcp.fab.title: What is ccassist MCP?
mcp.modal.intro.title: Give your CLI agents your chat history
mcp.modal.intro.lead: ccassist is a local MCP server. Register it once and any AI CLI — Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode — can search and reuse the sessions you already have, across every tool and project on this machine.
mcp.modal.intro.step1Desc: One click under "Client registration" writes the server into each CLI's config. Existing files are backed up first.
mcp.modal.intro.step2Desc: The ccassist skill teaches your agent when to reach for the tools, so you can ask in plain language instead of naming them.
mcp.modal.intro.step3Title: Restart the CLI, then just ask.
mcp.modal.intro.step3Desc: "Continue with my last Codex session", or "how did I fix that timezone bug last week?" — the agent pulls the context itself.
mcp.modal.intro.use1: Hand work from one CLI to another without re-explaining it.
mcp.modal.intro.use2: Recover the reasoning behind a change months later.
mcp.modal.intro.use3: Ask which past sessions touched a file, and what they changed.
mcp.modal.intro.note: Everything stays on 127.0.0.1 — your history never leaves this machine. One VS Code window serves the port; the others take over automatically when it closes.
mcp.modal.intro.footer: Reopen this any time from the "?" button.
mcp.modal.setup.title: Turn on ccassist
mcp.modal.setup.footer: Config files are backed up before any change.
mcp.setup.step1Enabled: ccassist is already serving on 127.0.0.1. Nothing to do here.
mcp.setup.step1Disabled: Turns on claude-history.mcp.enabled and binds the port on 127.0.0.1. You can switch it off any time from Settings above.
mcp.setup.step2Note: Adds an "ccassist" MCP entry to each config file.
mcp.setup.step3Note: Optional, but it is what lets you ask in plain language instead of naming tools.
mcp.setup.footer: After this finishes, restart each CLI (or reload its MCP servers) so it picks up the new registration.
